questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The culture of Ireland and trinity as a historic university

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was alright, there was not a lot information to get, but the most important was easy to find.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I changed my modules and that was very easy and the administration are helpful

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Very hard. I ended up renting an apartment through airbnb with my friend (from Denmark as well). If you are alone I would recommend to start early and take what you can get, because everything is gone in no time.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It's expensive. Housing in Dublin is expensive for everyone.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Erasmus students cannot get housing through the trinity, but I think there is help to get through trinity to find accommodation off campus.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Trinity send out forms beforehand, where you have to choose the modules you want. Then you will know which you get upon arrival. Otherwise trinity sent out emails with different information (how to get your student card, how to register at their platform, etc.). You just have to follow the steps, and none of it is important that you have fully completed berfore arrival.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There is an erasmus office at campus, and the school of law administration is also very helpful.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very succesful. I got everuthing I wanted and could even change for something else.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I would read about the type of exam for the different modules and the work load. Some of the modules are for freshman year and requires a bit more work.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The courses are easier than at UCPH

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: They only do lectures (the freshman year modules also have seminars) for 3 hours a week and then you just have to study on your own. They do more essay exams.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Public International Law, Medical Law and Ethics, Commercial Law

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend the modules with essay exams (commercial law and medical law).

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: The sports center was 79 euros, but for the whole semester. On the other hand you do not have to buy books, since you can rent them at the library.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food is a bit less expensive than expected, and the public transport is very cheap. But drinking and eating out was more expensive than expected. And then the housing was very expensive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I joined the swimming team, which was really fun and a good way to meet others and more Irish people. They have a lot of different sports, so there should be something for everyone.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend to join a lot of societies. You pay 2-3 euros to join a society, but then you can get offers for different trips around Ireland and fun nights with pubcrawl etc.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Travel. Dublin is a great city, but the whole country is so beautiful. Some areas and towns are easy to get to with train, but is also not expensive to rent a car, which is very recommended.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy. The Irish are very open at pubs.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join the sports teams, meet them at the pubs or trinity's bar, go on dates

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The relaxed vibe that Ireland and Dublin has. There is no rush, and they always have time for a beer at the pub. Very friendly and kind people.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Choose modules with essay exams. Join the intro week! and then join sports teams and societies. Travel around Ireland.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: To live in another country, meet new people from around the world, enjoy the irish culture and scenery.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Finding accommodation and neglecting my exams.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
